races.name: Racing TV Club Day EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Welcome Racing TV Club Members Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Concert Pitch
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's consistent performer carries Brian Robinson and arrives just two days off a run — five placed efforts in similar going underline his aptitude for these conditions, and his prominent style maps perfectly to the race shape Mrs Mole creates; top shortlist candidate.
runners_data.comment: Concert Pitch has been a model of consistency, finishing second in three of his last four starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions — stall three, carrying 135 lb, and our rating of 73 marks him clear at the head of this field, though he'll need to convert that placed form into something more on just two days' rest.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.note: Showed improvement when third over 5f on good ground and Harry Russell takes the ride; races from hold-up position but headgear (p) may sharpen his early response, and 20 days since last run leaves him fresh enough for a bold showing.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and returning in good time on 20 days' rest, Enemy Action has experience of today's trip and conditions and rates 6 lb above his official mark — the chief concern is that he remains winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Mrs Mole
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner here — Clifford Lee can dictate entirely on her terms over 5f, and while her form is modest (best effort a fourth), uncontested control of the pace is a legitimate asset; three outings on good or similar ground provide solid going compatibility.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out yet winless in her last three starts overall, Mrs Mole at least has experience of today's distance and going to call upon; 130 lb from stall eight is the challenge to overcome.

runners_data.name: Mardy Bum
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's two-year-old has placed twice in five good-ground runs and Mark Winn rides; a genuine hold-up type by inclination whose consistent efforts at this trip suggest he handles the surface, and he is one of the more credible challengers if the pace shapes up to suit a finisher from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Mardy Bum does have experience over today's trip and going in her favour, yet that unplaced effort last time out is hard to ignore; drawn in stall ten and carrying 130 lb, she looks a mid-division prospect at best.

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly carries a winner's profile — one win in seven on good ground — and Duran Fentiman knows Easterby's juveniles well; sits prominent by style and that is exactly where the race looks set to be won, making her a live player for the minor honours at minimum.
runners_data.comment: Lairy Mary has run over today's trip and going, and her win in recent starts shows she can find the line — but that solitary success among six outings is the concern, and she'll need to improve sharply on her latest sixth.

runners_data.name: Kaiulani Spirit
runners_data.note: No wins from three starts and no placed effort on similar going, with David Allan on board; headgear noted (b) but form figures of 675 do not inspire, and her chance appears limited unless the race produces an unusually strong pace that brings the back markers into play.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Kaiulani Spirit does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 29 days off should have him fresh; however, that uninspiring recent sequence of fifth, seventh and sixth makes it hard to fancy him strongly from stall two off 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Johns Power
runners_data.note: Roger Fell sends this youngster out 29 days fresh with Joanna Mason in the saddle; a genuine hold-up horse by running style whose chance is tempered by being mapped to midfield here — in a likely steady-run 5f affair he will struggle to manufacture the late momentum he naturally needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Johns Power faces a stiff task here; he does have experience over today's trip and going, and 29 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but that may be his strongest card.

runners_data.name: Targa
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's charge has five runs at this trip on good ground and showed a placed effort — Luke Morris is a quality booking — but this horse's natural instinct to race from the rear is compromised in a field with too many hold-up types chasing the same ground; style fit is discounted accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Targa shaped with promise when third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 65 suggests she holds strong claims; yet to score in her last five starts, and a trainer firing at just 3% is the significant concern.

runners_data.name: Good Fighter
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed/Jose Santos-trained juvenile wearing headgear (b) with Tom Kiely-Marshall claiming 5lbs; form figures of 759 on varied ground are uninspiring, and as a true hold-up runner mapped to midfield by necessity, the structural fit for this pace shape is poor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a ninth last time out the most damning evidence, Good Fighter faces a stiff task here; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but he's hard to fancy at these weights from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Articulate
runners_data.note: William Pyle rides for Kevin & Lauren Frost and a finishing tendency to fade, combined with the lowest official rating in the field at OR 45; a natural hold-up type placed into midfield by the volume of closers in this race, and the fade flag makes it hard to see a winning shape emerging here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of eighths his most recent returns, Articulate looks hard to fancy here despite having run over today's trip and going before — ranked last on our figures, he faces a stiff task from stall four carrying 115 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Mrs Mole is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner nursery and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she will stride to the front unchallenged from the outset and set a controlled, manageable gallop on good-to-firm ground over the minimum trip at Beverley. Concert Pitch and Lairy Mary will push to sit prominently behind her, making it a race with a compact early order but no true pace battle. The result is a steadily-run affair where the front two furlongs will be covered at sustainable tempo, compressing the field and reducing the premium on finishing speed alone — this shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce without needing a gap to open late. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely settle at the rear; Johns Power, Targa, Good Fighter and Articulate are all true hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map because they cannot all get their natural position, with Johns Power and Targa the most likely among them to secure a workable berth, but none will enjoy the unobstructed late run their style demands in a race likely to be won from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mrs Mole Leads, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mrs Mole dictates a steady pace and the race is won by a horse tracking her from the front two positions.
scenarios.body: Mrs Mole controls the tempo from flag to finish, ensuring the field bunches behind her and no late surge materialises; Concert Pitch or Lairy Mary, both mapped prominent, are ideally placed to strike at the two-furlong pole and hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Mrs Mole's steady, uncontested gallop on fast ground is slow enough that she conserves energy and outstays all challengers.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied early, Mrs Mole effectively dictates every stride and arrives at the final furlong with reserves intact; on good-to-firm Beverley ground she could simply prove too good for those attempting to reel her in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly quicker than expected and a horse travelling well mid-division picks its moment to challenge over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Should the leaders overdo it even marginally, a horse tracking in midfield with cover could produce a winning run; Mardy Bum, who has shown consistent placed form and holds genuine midfield pace, is best placed among this group to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the final furlong and a wide-open finish allows a true hold-up type to mow down a weakening leader.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses that have been redistributed out of their natural position actually finding clear daylight late, which is structurally unlikely given how the field maps; Targa or Johns Power would need everything to fall perfectly to land a blow from deep.

watchPoints.text: Mrs Mole is the only front-runner — if Clifford Lee jumps cleanly and establishes the rail, the race could be over before the field organises itself, so watch the break and the first two furlongs for any unexpected pressure from Concert Pitch or Lairy Mary.
Concert Pitch arrives on just two days' rest; watch whether he travels smoothly early or shows signs of fatigue, as his prominent position makes his condition in-running critical to the race shape.

Lairy Mary has won once over 5f on good ground and Tim Easterby's yard is firing (5 wins in 14 days) — if she quickens into the lead before the furlong marker she could steal a march on a field loaded with hold-up horses who cannot respond.

Johns Power, Targa, Good Fighter and Articulate are all genuine hold-up types competing for limited space at the rear; watch how their riders adapt in the opening furlong — any jostling or traffic behind a slow-pace leader could effectively end their chances before the race develops.

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed across all Beverley races on the card — if anything, the surface is riding fast, which will compress finishing times and reduce the advantage of any late challenge, reinforcing the front-prominent bias of this pace shape.

races.name: Hornsea Ladies At The Races Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Recent form reads 53665 and all five career runs have come at 5f-6f, so this 7½f trip is an obvious stamina question; a genuine late-runner by nature whose true hold-up style means gaining a clear position off a modest pace will be difficult with so many rivals seeking the same rear ground.|

runners_data.name: Court Legend
runners_data.note: Runs off 60 and carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag, with three runs all ending in double-figure finishes over 6f on Good; no visible evidence of the stamina or positional nous to cope better over an extra 1½f here.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last three starts, Court Legend has going experience in his favour and lines up from stall two carrying 132 lb; the consistent mid-table rating suggests he retains some ability, but recent unplaced efforts make improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Beach
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's runner showed a career-best 3rd last time and holds Good-ground form, but as a natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield map slot, actually getting a clean run through a congested field is the central challenge to landing the race.|
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Beach shaped with promise when third last time out and, back on familiar going after just 20 days, she looks a leading danger off an official rating of 59 — though she remains winless in her last four and must convert that placed effort into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Bonjour Belle
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison has had only 2 winners from 16 runners in the last 14 days, and this filly ran just six days ago; she's raced seven times at 7f and shows some staying power, but her authentic running style will have her buried further back than her mapped position implies, limiting her options if the pace is controlled.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Bonjour Belle faces a stiff task ranked eighth of ten on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly on just six days' rest.

runners_data.name: Ariane Sky
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good last time out at 135 RPR — the highest-rated horse in the field — and is the race's lone confirmed front-runner; James Owen's yard is in decent form (7/48 in 14 days), and with nothing to challenge her early, she commands this race from the front on these conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Ariane Sky won last time out and, having experience of today's trip and conditions, she looks a leading threat here; the main risk is whether she can confirm that latest victory carrying 135 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Returns after a 56-day absence for Craig Lidster (0/8 in 14 days) but ran second over 6f on Good last time and holds solid Good-ground form (4 from 4 in similar conditions); needs to find positioning improvement stepping to 7½f as a natural hold-up type.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, State Of Gold nonetheless shaped with promise when second last time out, and she has experience of today's going — carrying 135 lb from stall seven, the 56-day break may have freshened her for a big run here.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: The form book here reads better than most — 1W4P from 7-8 runs on Good ground, including wins and places over 7f-8f, and she is currently fit off a 6-day turnaround for Brian Ellison; her comfort at this trip and on this surface makes her the most naturally suited hold-up rival to the leader.|
runners_data.comment: Amantha arrives in fine nick, third last time out and a runner-up three starts back, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour; the chief concern is whether she can defy 134 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Farndale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends this 2-year-old back after 40 days off; career form of 6585 at 7f-8f on Good and Soft shows no wins and no places, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflecting how far out of natural role she'll race, finding the first two looks a tall order without a significant step forward.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Farndale has experience of today's trip and going, but placings of fifth, eighth, fifth and sixth suggest consistency at the wrong end of the field; the 40-day absence and 126 lb from stall ten are further questions she must answer.

runners_data.name: Wells Fargo Stage
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag, has finished 9th, 5th and 10th across three runs, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 signals she won't be travelling as close to the pace as her position on the map suggests; Tim Easterby's runner arrives after 38 days away with little to recommend her at this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Wells Fargo Stage at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and 38 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; a ninth last time out, however, leaves plenty to prove from stall five off 124 lb.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Dream
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's filly returns after 47 days off with form reading 570 — 11th, 7th and 5th across three runs — and at OR=48 is the lowest-rated runner in the race; out of role at the mapped position and with no wins or places to her name, this trip over 7½f on fast ground is likely to stretch her.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Yorkshire Dream faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's going before and the 47-day break at least means he returns fresh, but the recent string of unplaced efforts makes him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Whisper Angel
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish tag and has finished 8th, 10th and 7th across her three runs; Nigel Tinkler's runner was last seen 13 days ago and at OR=45 faces the toughest task in the field, with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 confirming she is unlikely to race in a position that gives her a realistic late run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with an eighth and a seventh among recent efforts, Whisper Angel is hard to fancy ranked last on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 13 days between runs suggests she is at least fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Ariane Sky is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner nursery over 7½f on Good to Firm ground at Beverley, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without burning energy in a contested early duel. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up or midfield in style — Claret And Blues, Sovereign Beach, Bonjour Belle, Farndale, Wells Fargo Stage, Yorkshire Dream and Whisper Angel are all genuine hold-up types redistributed forward on the map simply because the rear positions are oversubscribed; in reality, several of them will be unable to travel as prominently as their mapped positions suggest. With Ariane Sky able to control tempo from the front and Good to Firm ground placing a premium on relaxed travel and mid-race conserved energy, this race shape strongly favours front-running or prominent profiles — Ariane Sky herself and the handful of genuinely prominent-to-midfield types who track the tempo without being swallowed by a congested back group are best positioned. The overwhelming hold-up bias in this field means true closers face a tactical headache: if Ariane Sky sets only a fair gallop, there is no compression of pace late on to suit those coming from furthest back, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the clear tactical winner today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ariane Sky Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Ariane Sky bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but honest pace, controlling every yard from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: She dictates on her own terms on Good to Firm ground, conserving enough to quicken late, and the compact hold-up group behind cannot generate the sustained finish to reel her in over 7½f at Beverley's track configuration. Runners who sit just off the pace in a tracking role and have the fitness and form to strike from second or third are best placed to threaten.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Overhaul Her
scenarios.trigger: If Ariane Sky's early pace is fractionally too strong and she ties up inside the final furlong, leaving a prominent tracker to pounce.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third throughout, travelling well within itself, inherits the lead at the optimal moment and holds the weakening leader at bay on the fast surface. Amantha, with strong recent form at 7f-8f on Good ground and multiple placed efforts, is ideally suited to this shape, as is State Of Gold who returns from a layoff with a runner-up effort to recommend him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ariane Sky sets a stronger-than-expected gallop that stretches the field and creates genuine pace collapse in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up runner threads through to score late, though this shape is undermined by the fact that most of the nominal closers in this field are redistributed types who will not secure a genuine late-running position and face a congested midfield rather than clear daylight. Amantha, who has genuine back-to-front form credentials, is best-equipped among the hold-up group to benefit, though the scenario itself is the least structurally reliable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Interference Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant early crowding, positional shuffling or mid-race interference that disrupts Ariane Sky's rhythm and bunches the field.
scenarios.body: An unpredictable outcome emerges in which a lower-rated runner catches the field flat-footed at the finish, with the wide-open hold-up pack potentially producing a surprise from a fresher horse returning from a short break such as Bonjour Belle or Whisper Angel. However, given the one-dimensional pace map and Ariane Sky's strong recent win, this remains a low-probability outcome and should be treated as a market overlay check rather than a primary scenario.

watchPoints.text: Ariane Sky — watch whether Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) settles her cleanly in the first two furlongs; if she runs free or is pressed unexpectedly by any horse disputing the early lead, her chance of sustaining the gallop to the line is materially reduced.

Amantha — watch her position at the two-furlong marker; if Ben Robinson has her tracking in third or fourth at that point she is the likeliest horse to overhaul Ariane Sky late, given her proven 7f-8f form on Good ground across multiple placed efforts.

State Of Gold — watch for how sharply William Pyle gets him into a handy position off the 56-day break; returning from a layoff can mean a slow beginning, and if he misses the early kick he will be caught in the crowded hold-up group with no clear run.

Congestion at the rear — with seven or more genuine hold-up horses all seeking the back half of the field, watch for early crowding and positional elbowing between Farndale, Wells Fargo Stage, Yorkshire Dream and Whisper Angel, which could disrupt each other's rhythms and create traffic for Claret And Blues and Sovereign Beach.

Going — declared as Good to Firm for this race specifically per the going report; any horse with a significant soft-ground flag in its form should be viewed with caution, as the fast surface rewards relaxed travel and a clean stride, not grinding.

races.name: Connexin Super Fast Sprint Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who handles good ground well (8 of 11 runs on similar going, one win four places), but a 70-day absence with a 7lb claimer aboard is a flag; suited by a pace collapse rather than the controlled tempo Ingleby Archie is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Call To Action showed up with a second last time out and a winner four starts back, but the ninth two starts back is a blemish and 70 days off the track is a query; he has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is no featherweight at a rating of 75.

runners_data.name: Holbache
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer who drops to 5f from recent 6f runs for Julie Camacho, whose string is in form (1 win from 18 runners in 14 days); headgear flag (blinkers worn previously) and 54-day break worth checking, but racing style maps perfectly to the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Holbache won two starts back but has finished fifth last time out and rates well below the field on our figures, ranked 11 of 12; a 54-day break adds to the questions, though he has distance and going experience and breaks from stall one.

runners_data.name: Castan
runners_data.note: Shown as hold-up in style but sits on the prominent side of the map; recent form figures of 814096 are ragged and he has zero wins or places from 15 similar-going runs, making him hard to trust even if the pace shapes in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Castan arrives here just 12 days after his last outing, fit and ready, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour — his win five starts back shows he can land a blow on his day, though his recent sixth and ninth will need reversing.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's consistent 5f performer has an excellent recent course record (12 of 15 runs on similar going) and Jason Hart takes the ride; placed five times in similar company this season and will track the pace from a prominent position, giving him every chance in the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, American Bay nevertheless catches the eye with a second three starts back and a smart weight-adjusted rating of 83 that marks him out as the standout in this field; the chief concern is his fifth last time out suggesting peak form may be elusive.

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old who has been running respectably at this level (placed at 5f on good ground twice in last five) but has drifted back to a hold-up role; trainer Michael Herrington is in decent form (3/11 in 14 days), though the hold-up style is a disadvantage if the pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: A second three starts back hints at ability, but Good Earth has been out of the frame in his two most recent efforts and faces a stiff ask from 132 lb off stall nine; experience over today's trip and going gives him a foothold, yet consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field, with a clear record of going to the front on good and good-to-firm ground (12 of 15 similar-going runs); Jack Garritty knows the horse and the Beverley track suits a bold-going sort, making him the key pace-setter who shapes the entire race.
runners_data.comment: Ingleby Archie won three starts back and was third two starts back, showing he retains ability, but a fifth last time out tempers confidence; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 131 lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type who has finished in the frame three times in recent 5f runs on similar going but has not won in this sphere; David Nolan is a capable pilot but the redistribution pressure in this field means he will likely be closer than preferred, limiting his closing impact.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ventura Express nonetheless shaped with promise when fourth last time out and third six starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going; the risk is that a win has so far eluded him at this level.

runners_data.name: Squealer
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — his best form comes from off a fast pace — but with four redistributed hold-up types in this field, he will find himself further forward than his preferred berth; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) reflects the mismatch, and his chance is tempered accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and shaped with promise in recent starts, Squealer returns after 23 days in good order, and his experience over today's distance and going counts in his favour. Carrying 130 lb from stall five, he is preferred on his overall profile at this level, albeit yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Shazani
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who drops to 5f after promising 6f and 7f form, with a win and two seconds from last five starts for Roy Bowring; maps prominently and could be competitive if the step down in trip suits, with Lewis Edmunds a capable partner.
runners_data.comment: Shazani won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but he carries 130 lb from stall 2 and his recent record shows inconsistency — three finishes outside the places in his last six starts suggest he can be hard to catch right.

runners_data.name: Infinity Blue
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's five-year-old returns after a 304-day absence — a major fitness query — and is a true hold-up horse by inclination, yet will be unable to secure the deepest position in this busy field; the combination of layoff and positional compromise makes this a difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 304 days off the track, Infinity Blue is hard to fancy here; he does have experience over today's trip and going, and a third three starts back offers a crumb of hope, but he faces a stiff task from stall 8 off a mark of 65.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's eight-year-old has finished second twice in five recent 5f runs on good ground, but the redistribution context is critical here — his natural closing style cannot be fully deployed when pushed forward by the crowded hold-up group; James Sullivan will manage him as best he can but the race shape is not in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Jojo Rabbit has finished fourth last time out and sixth two starts back, with little recent encouragement — experience over today's trip and going at least removes two unknowns.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 57) with a mixed recent record on good ground and a cold trainer (0/2 in 14 days); a true hold-up type forced forward by redistribution pressure, carrying a tongue-tie, and facing a stiff class test — this combination makes her hard to support.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Opal Storm faces a stiff ask, and she was eighth latest; a win two starts back offers the one bright spot, though distance and going experience at least means conditions hold no fresh excuses.

races.paceDynamic: Ingleby Archie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 5f handicap at Beverley on good-to-firm ground, and with no genuine rival pressing from the gates, he is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo rather than being dragged into a gruelling speed duel. The prominent types — Holbache, American Bay, and Shazani — will track just off the pace, keeping the gallop honest without turning it into a true burn-up, which is the key structural feature of this race shape. Because the pace is solo and uncontested, the front portion of the field is unlikely to be softened up sufficiently to hand late closers a winning opportunity from deep, meaning the race strongly favours those racing in the first three to five positions throughout. This field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Squealer, Jojo Rabbit, Infinity Blue, and Opal Storm are genuine back-of-the-field horses who will be unable to secure their natural position in this traffic, with Squealer and Jojo Rabbit the most likely to find a few lengths of cover but still further forward than ideal; the tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can travel into the race from a handy pitch are best placed to exploit a single-paced front-runner setting a manageable tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Archie Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie leads without serious pressure and the pace is sustainable enough for prominent racers to travel comfortably and pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ingleby Archie sets a fair but not punishing tempo on good-to-firm ground, and the horses racing in his slipstream — Holbache, American Bay, and Shazani — get the perfect tow into the race before unleashing their finishing effort; with no true late burst required, the winner emerges from the prominent group that has been travelling sweetly throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie dictates fully unchallenged, finds a clear rail, and the pace proves too hot for those giving him weight in behind.
scenarios.body: With no rival prepared to seriously contest the early lead, Ingleby Archie secures a coveted position against the rail at Beverley and runs his rivals into the ground with a controlled but relentless gallop; his course form and willingness to front up make him the chief beneficiary when the race is run at his rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie goes too fast, the prominent horses overcook it tracking him, and the pace collapses to gift a late thrust.
scenarios.body: A frantic early clip would string the field out and leave the prominent trackers racing on empty inside the final two furlongs, opening a narrow window for a horse arriving from midfield with a run; Call To Action is best positioned among the true hold-up types to benefit, though note that several redistributed horses — Squealer and Jojo Rabbit — will be further forward than their natural style and thus less able to deliver the pure closing kick this shape demands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Ups Flatter
scenarios.trigger: If the race dissolves into a messy crawl and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish that suits arriving horses.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace would theoretically compress the field and give late movers a chance, but this scenario is heavily discounted because Squealer, Jojo Rabbit, Infinity Blue, and Opal Storm — the horses who would win this shape — are redistributed and will not be in their natural deep position to launch; the scenario is possible in theory but the personnel for it are racing out of role.

watchPoints.text: Ingleby Archie's tempo is the single most important factor in this race — if Jack Garritty controls the gallop and gets a clear lead against the Beverley rail, the entire field is racing to his tune and the race shape favours him and those immediately behind.

Holbache and American Bay are likely to contest the prominent positions directly behind Ingleby Archie, and any scrimmaging or interference between them in the early stages could unsettle either runner and hand an advantage to the cleaner traveller.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Squealer, Jojo Rabbit, Infinity Blue, and Opal Storm — will be jostling for position in the midfield rather than settling naturally at the rear; watch for early crowding on the stands side that could impede genuine prominent types trying to slot in.

Infinity Blue's 304-day absence is the longest layoff in the field by a significant margin; monitor paddock behaviour and early race demeanour, as a fit-again or rustier-than-expected return will materially affect how the midfield traffic plays out behind her.

Good-to-firm going is confirmed for this race across multiple reports, but several horses in the field carry headgear changes or have patchy records on faster ground — Holbache (hood) and Opal Storm (tongue-tie) are worth watching in the preliminaries for any signs of unsettlement.

races.name: Middle Distance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Return With Gold
runners_data.note: The key horse in this race tactically — sole confirmed front-runner who will control the pace unchallenged; Good to Firm ground suits (going=OK) but its OR=66 and recent form of 131-40 shows inconsistency, and the style-fit tag signals it is actually racing out of its most natural role here having come from a hold-up background, tempering confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Return With Gold was a winner three starts back and third four starts back, showing a likeable profile over today's trip, and returning fit after 19 days; the concern is his unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with three wins and three places in fifteen similar-going starts, but a genuine hold-up operator who in this traffic-heavy field has been pushed forward on the map from its natural rear-of-field berth; Ramsden-trained and fresh off just seven days' rest, the bounce risk is real and a clear run may prove elusive.|
runners_data.comment: Consecutive sevenths in his last two starts make Sisterandbrother hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, and a speed rating of 61 offers little encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going before, and there is winning form further back in the sequence.

runners_data.name: Grey Fable
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's six-year-old carries a tongue-tie and is at heart a hold-up horse, but with zero wins or places in eight runs on similar ground the form evidence is discouraging regardless of where it sits in the field; the redistribution to midfield flatters its likely race position.|
runners_data.comment: Grey Fable has experience of both today's trip and going, and a win four starts back shows he retains ability; at 133 lb, the weight is the single factor connections will be watching closely.

runners_data.name: Wardlaw
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old has a tidy profile — placed in three of seven Good-ground runs and twice finished second at exactly this trip on Good — and Luke Morris gives it a tactical edge; genuinely suited to holding up and waiting, it is one of the few here whose natural style is uncompromised by the race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Wardlaw has been a model of consistency, placing in three of his last four starts — second two runs back and third last time out — and he has run over today's trip before; the main risk is that 48 days off the track leaves his fitness under a question mark.

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride for Ed Dunlop on this three-year-old whose best recent run was a third at 1m4f on Good; six consecutive runs on Good ground with only one placing suggests it finds a way to be involved without winning, but the trip and conditions are familiar and it should get a clean sight of the front-runner.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, That Darn Cantor faces a stiff ask here, despite his third last time out offering a sliver of encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going before, and comes back quickly enough at 12 days.

runners_data.name: Mr Moonshine
runners_data.note: Fahey's three-year-old is at its core a hold-up horse, yet the overcrowded rear of the field means it is shown in midfield on the map — a position that is not where it will naturally want to be; Oisin Orr has the skill to adapt, but three places from eight similar-going starts and no wins make it vulnerable even in a favourable shape.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in good heart, Mr Moonshine has finished third last time out and second the time before, and he has experience over today's trip and going — our rating of 77 marks him as the one to beat here, though he remains winless in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Return With Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and will stride into the lead from the outset over this 1m4f trip at Beverley, almost certainly uncontested and able to dictate a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground. With no other natural leader to apply pressure, the pace is likely to be honest but controlled, giving Return With Gold every opportunity to conserve energy and kick again in the straight. The field behind is dominated by hold-up types — Wardlaw, That Darn Cantor, Sisterandbrother, Grey Fable, and Mr Moonshine all want to come from off the pace — meaning the race shape strongly favours a front-runner who can steal a march and a finisher with the tactical speed to close on a steady-run race. Three of those hold-up runners (Mr Moonshine, Sisterandbrother, Grey Fable) are redistributed into midfield on the map because the true rear of the field is overcrowded, but their natural instinct remains to settle and close; the horses most likely to actually secure the early prominent berths behind Return With Gold are Wardlaw and That Darn Cantor by process of elimination.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Return With Gold is allowed to coast in front at a measured tempo and the hold-up pack fails to reel it in.
scenarios.body: Return With Gold settles into an uncontested lead, controls the fractions on Good to Firm ground, and simply has too much in reserve when the closers make their move late in the straight. A field full of natural hold-up horses with no pace-pressing rivals means the leader is never truly tested and can dictate the winning move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late closers swamp leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Return With Gold proves genuinely slow, compressing the finish and nullifying its lead.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race collapses into a sprint finish off the home turn, negating any advantage for the front-runner and rewarding whoever can quicken sharpest from a tracking position. Wardlaw, who has placed repeatedly at this trip on Good ground, and That Darn Cantor, with solid form at 1m4f, are best positioned to produce a winning late burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield stalker pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types overcomes its unnatural position and delivers a telling run from a midfield slot.
scenarios.body: Mr Moonshine or Sisterandbrother, forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, could benefit if the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften up the front-runner while they track in a prominent enough position to strike. However, this shape depends on horses operating outside their comfort zone, making it a lower-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — no clear shape
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up pack bunches, jostles for position, and the race fractures into a ragged contest with no clean run for any runner.
scenarios.body: A messy tactical race where multiple closers interfere with each other's runs could produce an unexpected result, potentially benefiting Grey Fable or a horse that finds a clear passage through.

watchPoints.text: Return With Gold's early sectionals — if it is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first half-mile, it becomes very difficult to catch in a field devoid of natural pace-pressers.

Wardlaw's draw and early position — Sir Mark Prescott's runner is the most likely horse to track the leader in a genuine stalking spot; watch whether Luke Morris parks it close enough to pounce in the straight rather than too far back in a falsely-run race.

Congestion among the hold-up pack in the early stages — with four or five horses all wanting to settle towards the rear, there is a real risk of interference or a compromised run for multiple closers rounding the home turn.

That Darn Cantor's starting price — Cieren Fallon is a significant booking for Ed Dunlop and any market support here should be noted given its consistent recent form at the course and distance conditions.

Grey Fable's going record — eight runs on similar ground without a win or place is a persistent concern, and despite being competitive in other conditions, it should be monitored for any signs of disengagement on the Good to Firm surface.

races.name: Racing Again On Saturday 29 August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here with Roy Bowring's operation in modest form (1/3 over 14 days); has won off this mark before but recent form reads 8-3-1-4-0-6, his sim-going record is weak (0W0P in 5 tries), and at age 9 this is a career low — his chance rests entirely on controlling a pace no one challenges.|
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out and unplaced two starts back make for a patchy recent spell, though a winner four starts back shows ability; he has experience over today's trip and going, and the 133 lb burden is the chief concern here.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's ten-year-old has excellent course-relevant form — four of his last five runs at 8f on Good or Soft, placing twice — and Joanna Mason takes the ride; he races prominently and is perfectly placed to track the leader in what should be a truly run race for horses at the head of affairs.|
runners_data.comment: Copper And Five has shown enough ability in his recent starts, landing a pair of runner-up finishes and a fourth in there — he has run over today's trip and going, carries 132 lb from stall four, and a 54 rating suggests he's ahead of his official mark. The risk is that he's winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ten Sixty Six
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has placed three times in nine similar-going runs and Mark Winn rides; a hold-up type who needs a proper gallop to launch from off the pace, and the expected moderate tempo under Back From Dubai is not ideal for his style.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Ten Sixty Six does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 33 days off gives her a fresh look; but a best recent finish of fourth and a rating of 53 suggest she'll need to find improvement to trouble the principals from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Dumfries
runners_data.note: James Sullivan partners this Ruth Carr-trained six-year-old who has been consistent without winning (0W from 15 sim-going runs, but 3W overall and 4 places); a hold-up horse who needs a race run to suit closers, which this shape may not fully provide, though his stamina for the trip is not in question.|
runners_data.comment: Dumfries arrives here 16 days fresh, carrying 138 lb from stall eight, and has run over today's trip and going before; winless in his last five starts, but our rating just edges him ahead of these rivals and he shapes as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Amarachi
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the mount on this Joseph Parr four-year-old who has been absent 167 days — the longest layoff in the field and a significant fitness concern; placed four times from five runs on Tapeta rather than turf, and his Going sim-rating of just 2 runs makes his turf form difficult to assess.|
runners_data.comment: Twice a runner-up in recent starts, Amarachi has run over today's trip and going and her rating of 57 marks her as a genuine danger from stall 3 — though winless in her last five starts, and 167 days off the track is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Daragh Bourke's three-year-old won last time out over 8f on Good and has a live Each-Way profile, but Shane Gray rides and the horse's natural style is deep hold-up — pushed into a midfield berth on the map because the field is overloaded with rear-runners, and genuine pace pressure at the front is unlikely to produce the searching gallop he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Saxon Grace won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but she's back just five days later carrying 134 lb, and her inconsistent recent form — unplaced and down the field in several of her last six starts — suggests she's as likely to disappoint as to follow up.

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: William Pyle partners Mike Sowersby's four-year-old, whose recent form includes a creditable 4th in a 16-runner handicap over 16f; she has been running over considerably longer trips — 10f to 16f — and dropping to 1m½f on Good to Firm is an untested scenario, with zero wins or places in 5 sim-going runs; her natural hold-up style finds her in a midfield slot here that doesn't reflect her true racing position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with three unplaced efforts among recent outings and a modest speed rating of 50, Sweet Cicely faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going, and 25 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: Faye McManoman rides for Brian Rothwell and this four-year-old is tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a significant flag in a race where closers need a strong late pace to launch into; all five recent runs have been over 5-6f on Good, suggesting this 1m½f trip is substantially longer than her optimum distance, and her hold-up style is redistributed into midfield due to overcrowding at the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with back-to-back ninth-place finishes among a string of disappointing efforts, Aurora's Doublesix faces a stiff ask carrying 129 lb from stall six, and a speed rating of 51 does little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Royal Sizzler
runners_data.note: Sean Kirrane takes the ride on Michael Dods' three-year-old, who has just one run in similar going conditions from four career starts; a natural hold-up type placed into midfield on the map because of the overcrowded rear group — 51 days off and limited form data make him one of the harder horses to assess, with no wins or places in sim-going.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with two unplaced efforts among them, Royal Sizzler faces a stiff ask from a trainer firing at just 3% in the last 14 days; she has run over today's trip and going before, but an official mark of 50 against a rating of 42 makes her very hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Harswell River
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old is ridden by apprentice Cian Horgan (5lb claim) and boasts four places from nine runs including two at 10f on Good — the most comparable trip in the field for a horse at the hold-up end of the spectrum; though pushed into midfield here due to overcrowding of rear-runners, his recent 17-day turnaround suggests he is in a good place, and the claimer's allowance helps under his 125lb weight.|
runners_data.comment: Harswell River ran second two starts back and third five starts back, showing she's capable of mixing it at this level, and our rating of 56 puts her right in the mix despite being yet to win in recent starts — the main concern is her 125 lb burden from stall 10.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the one confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press him for the lead from flag-fall, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. The pace note confirms he will not be pressured, meaning the tempo is likely to be steady-to-moderate early before quickening in the home straight — a shape that strongly rewards horses who can travel prominently and kick, rather than deep hold-up types needing a truly searching gallop to close. Copper And Five, the other prominent runner, is the natural challenger for the position just behind the leader, and these two are best placed to exploit the race shape as it develops. Five of the remaining runners — Saxon Grace, Royal Sizzler, Harswell River, Sweet Cicely and Aurora's Doublesix — are true hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield on the map because there are more off-the-pace types than can realistically race at the rear; Saxon Grace and Harswell River, based on recent form, are the most likely of that group to actually secure a forward position, but even they face a tactical disadvantage. The verdict is clear: this race shape suits prominent-raced horses who can track a lone front-runner and strike early in the straight, with deep closers disadvantaged by the likely lack of a searching gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai goes unchallenged to the front and controls a steady-to-moderate tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Back From Dubai sets an uncontested pace and, without any horse willing to go with him, he conserves energy through the race before picking up again in Beverley's home straight; horses who can travel close to him without expending energy — Copper And Five in particular — are best placed to capitalise if he tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Copper And Five or another horse pushes Back From Dubai into a slightly faster early tempo than he would prefer.
scenarios.body: A more genuinely-run pace drags the field into the race earlier and stretches the field, meaning the stamina of horses who stay well at this trip comes into play in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically late and redistributed hold-up horses get an unusually clear run through from midfield.
scenarios.body: Even in this scenario, most of the horses shown in midfield are not natural closers but redistributed hold-up types operating out of their ideal role, limiting the reliability of a late finish; Dumfries and Ten Sixty Six, who have the most credible form profiles in this region, are the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wins Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai dictates completely unchallenged and is never headed, winning wire-to-wire without being caught.
scenarios.body: A very weak overall pace field means he simply never faces a challenge and his rivals cannot find the gears to reel him in up the straight; this scenario is less likely given his modest recent form in similar conditions.

watchPoints.text: Back From Dubai controls the entire race shape — if he gets away cleanly and faces no pressure, the tempo will be slow enough to compromise every hold-up horse in the field, and Copper And Five is the only horse with the position and profile to threaten him.|

Aurora's Doublesix is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish and is running over a trip (1m½f) far longer than her recent 5-6f starts — she could stop quickly in the home straight and cause interference for horses coming from midfield.|

Amarachi has not run for 167 days and all his placed form has come on Tapeta (artificial) rather than Good to Firm turf — connections face a significant unknown on both fitness and surface suitability going into this race.|

The apprentice claim of 5lb for Cian Horgan on Harswell River is worth monitoring; at 125lbs he carries the lightest weight in the race and if the hold-up types get any late run at all, a lightened burden over the final furlong on Beverley's uphill finish could be meaningful.|

Ruth Carr has two runners — Copper And Five and Dumfries — which creates potential stable tactics interest; if Copper And Five is the yard's primary hope, Dumfries's rider James Sullivan may be instructed to press the pace and soften the race up for his stablemate.|
